name: lmtest
resume: All 23 exports of lmtest 0.9-40 are checked on a linear model. The Durbin-Watson probability is Farebrother's pan in the Rust crate. F, chi-square, and t tails use SciPy. The Cox normal tail uses extraDistr's math.erf. Granger lags use zoo's lag and merge. Harrison-McCabe draws use extraDistr's normal generator on boot's Mersenne-Twister. glm, mlm, and survreg methods are not in the exports that were checked.

functions.name: dwtest
functions.done: Durbin-Watson statistic. The exact probability is Farebrother's pan.
functions.not_done: order.by as a formula is a numeric vector.

check.case: Exact Durbin-Watson statistic and p-value, 20 observations.

proof.r:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(lmtest))
x <- c(1,3,2,6,5,8,7,4,9,10,12,11,15,13,14,18,16,19,17,20)
y <- c(2,2,4,3,7,6,9,8,5,11,10,14,12,16,15,13,19,17,20,18)
z <- sqrt(x)
one <- function() {
d <- dwtest(y ~ x)
paste(sprintf("%.17g", c(d$statistic, d$p.value)), collapse=",")
}

value <- one()
elapsed <- numeric(20)
for (i in seq_len(20)) {
  t0 <- as.numeric(Sys.time())
  one()
  elapsed[[i]] <- as.numeric(Sys.time()) - t0
}
shown <- enc2utf8(paste(as.character(value), collapse = "|"))
shown <- gsub("\n", " / ", shown, fixed = TRUE)
cat("VALUE ", shown, "\n", sep = "")
cat(sprintf("MS %.17g\n", median(elapsed) * 1000))
proof.python:
from lmtest import dwtest
import numpy as np
x = np.array([1,3,2,6,5,8,7,4,9,10,12,11,15,13,14,18,16,19,17,20], float)
y = np.array([2,2,4,3,7,6,9,8,5,11,10,14,12,16,15,13,19,17,20,18], float)
z = np.sqrt(x)

def one():
    d = dwtest(y, x)
    return f"{d['statistic']:.17g},{d['p_value']:.17g}"

import statistics
import time
value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print("VALUE " + str(value).replace("\n", " / "))
print(f"MS {statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")

functions.name: coxtest
functions.done: Cox statistics for y on x against y on sqrt(x). The normal tail is math.erf.

check.case: Both Cox rows: estimate, standard error, z, and two-sided p-value.

proof.python:
from lmtest import coxtest
import numpy as np
x = np.array([1,3,2,6,5,8,7,4,9,10,12,11,15,13,14,18,16,19,17,20], float)
y = np.array([2,2,4,3,7,6,9,8,5,11,10,14,12,16,15,13,19,17,20,18], float)
z = np.sqrt(x)

def one():
    c = coxtest(y, x, z)
    rows = np.column_stack([c["estimate"], c["std_error"], c["z"], c["p_value"]])
    return ",".join(f"{v:.17g}" for v in rows.reshape(-1))

import statistics
import time

elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)

print(f"MS {statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")

from lmtest import raintest
import numpy as np
x = np.array([1,3,2,6,5,8,7,4,9,10,12,11,15,13,14,18,16,19,17,20], float)
y = np.array([2,2,4,3,7,6,9,8,5,11,10,14,12,16,15,13,19,17,20,18], float)
z = np.sqrt(x)

def one():
    r = raintest(y, x)
    return f"{r['statistic']:.17g},{r['parameter'][0]:.17g},{r['parameter'][1]:.17g},{r['p_value']:.17g}"

import statistics
import time
value = one()
elapsed = []
for _ in range(20):
    started = time.perf_counter()
    one()
    elapsed.append((time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
print("VALUE " + str(value).replace("\n", " / "))
print(f"MS {statistics.median(elapsed):.17g}")
